name: Women's suffrage movement
title: The story of the women’s suffrage movement

text: For most of history, voting belonged to men, and usually to men who owned property.
In England, Mary Wollstonecraft argued that women deserved the same education as men.
src: For most of history, voting, where it existed at all, belonged to men, and usually to men of property
In England Mary Wollstonecraft’s A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792) argued that women were rational beings who deserved the same education as men

text: More than 170 years ago, women and men met at Seneca Falls in New York to demand the vote for women.
Their declaration said “that all men and women are created equal”.
src: The Seneca Falls Convention in New York adopts the Declaration of Sentiments, which demands the vote for women
declared “that all men and women are created equal”

text: Susan B. Anthony organised and gave talks for the cause for half a century.
She was arrested for voting in 1872, and she refused to pay her fine.
src: Susan B. Anthony, a veteran of the temperance and anti-slavery campaigns, organised and lectured for half a century
arrested for voting in the presidential election of 1872, she was fined $100 at her trial in 1873 and refused to pay

text: In 1893 New Zealand became the first self-governing country to give all adult women the vote.
Kate Sheppard had organised petitions, long lists of names asking Parliament to give women the vote.
src: won its first national victory in New Zealand in 1893 / New Zealand becomes the first self-governing country to give all adult women the vote
petitions organised by Kate Sheppard and the Women’s Christian Temperance Union persuaded Parliament

text: In Britain, the suffragettes of Emmeline Pankhurst smashed windows and refused to eat in prison, a hunger strike.
Much of Europe and North America gave women the vote around the First World War.
src: Emmeline Pankhurst founds the Women’s Social and Political Union in Manchester / in Britain the militant suffragettes smashed windows, set fires and went on hunger strike in prison
Much of Europe and North America gave women the vote around the First World War

text: But many women of colour, and people in lands ruled as colonies, waited decades longer.
Today a statue of Millicent Garrett Fawcett, a leader of the movement, stands in Parliament Square in London.
src: but many women of colour and colonial subjects waited decades longer
the statue of Millicent Garrett Fawcett unveiled in Parliament Square in London in 2018, the first statue of a woman there / Millicent Garrett Fawcett the non-militant National Union
